title: Health Insurance for Parents in India: 9 Things to Check Before You Buy
intro: Medical costs rise every year and parents are the most likely to need care. A plan that looks cheap can leave you stuck at claim time. Here is what to compare.

p: Policies have a waiting period for pre-existing conditions, often two to four years. Look for the shortest one.
A cap on room rent can reduce the whole claim proportionately. Choose a plan with no cap or a high one.
Some plans for senior citizens make you pay a percentage of every claim. Know it before buying.
Check that the hospitals near your parents are in the cashless network.
Read the limits on cataract, joint replacement and other common treatments, and the list of exclusions.
Compare the insurer's claim settlement ratio and how long claims usually take.
A restoration benefit refills the cover after a claim. A super top-up adds more cover cheaply on top of a base plan.
Declare every health condition. Hiding one is the most common reason for rejection.
Premiums paid for parents may qualify for a deduction under Section 80D, under the old tax regime. Check the current limits.

faq.q: Should parents have their own policy?
faq.a: Often yes, a separate policy keeps their cover from being used up by the rest of the family.
Early. Premiums rise with age and conditions can appear later.

disclaimer: Note: this is general information, not financial or investment advice. Rules, limits and prices change, so check current details and speak to a qualified adviser before deciding.
